summary: Split credential pool fanout causing intermittent priority-lane 429s for background workers
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataStream Labs reports intermittent 429s affecting low-priority background workers (bulk-embed pipeline) while interactive, high-priority streams remained healthy. Errors started after a staged credential split the customer began using ephemeral worker keys for background consumers and a long-lived key for interactive sessions.

Impact:
- ~8-12% of background jobs failing with 429s during peak ingest windows (12:00-15:00 PDT).
- Customer-visible increased job retries and longer overall pipeline completion times.
- No reported impact to interactive chat endpoints but degraded throughput for bulk pipelines.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (tenant dedicated) in prod-us-west (us-west-2).
- Customer uses a mix of ephemeral short-lived credentials for orchestrated workers and a stable API key for interactive traffic.

Observed behavior:
- 429s include throttle headers referencing "priority-lane" and show rapid refill depletion for that lane.
- Logs show bursts of token accounting attributed to ephemeral keys immediately after worker orchestration rollouts.

Expected behavior:
- Background workers should be accounted against a separate background/bulk quota lane and not exhaust priority lane credit used by interactive sessions.

Customer notes:
- They started rolling ephemeral credentials on 2026-03-10 as part of a rollout to scale worker fleets. 429s began 2026-03-11 19:05 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a tenant with a dedicated pool and two credential classes: long-lived interactive key + ephemeral bulk worker keys.
2) Start a mix of interactive sessions (low QPS) and parallel bulk embedding jobs using ephemeral credentials (high parallelism).
3) Trigger a rolling restart of worker orchestrator to rotate ephemeral keys in 5s batches.
4) Observe rate-limit headers on bulk requests and count 429s.

Notes: Repro is timing-dependent; we hit the issue reliably when many ephemeral keys are created within a short window and route-weighting is non-zero for priority lanes.
logs:
Sample throttle header snapshot (prod-us-west):
- X-RateLimit-Lane: priority-lane
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
- X-RateLimit-Reset: 18
- X-RateLimit-Window: 60s

Metric snapshots: priority_lane_refill_rate dropped from 1000 tokens/min to 40 tokens/min over 90s during rollout; token-burn spiked by 6x compared to baseline.

2026-03-11 21:05 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Confirmed 429 pattern in ingress logs. Early hypothesis: ephemeral key fanout caused per-key accounting to be attributed to priority lane due to route-canonicalization mismatch at edge. Escalating to rate-limiter owners.

2026-03-12 02:40 - Samir Gupta (Rate-limiter): Found edge proxy was normalizing route paths for signed ephemeral keys; normalization dropped a query-string tag that distinguishes bulk vs interactive paths causing requests to be grouped under priority-lane. Added correlation logs and an incrementing debug flag for affected tenant.

2026-03-12 10:15 - Customer (DataStream Labs - Ops): Confirmed they pushed a large worker replumb with short TTL keys at 19:00 UTC. Asked if a config change could be applied to avoid impacting interactive lane.

2026-03-12 16:30 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Applied temporary mitigation: reclassify ephemeral key namespace to background lane server-side for tenant datastream. Monitoring for 24h. Asked engineering to prepare a patch to canonicalization logic.
2026-03-13 08:00 - Asha Patel (Support): Customer reports background job success rate improved to >99% after mitigation. Scheduled change window for patch rollout (2026-03-14).

investigation_notes:
Summary of investigation:
- Reproduction correlated 429 events with bursts of ephemeral key creation.
- Root cause: edge proxy canonicalization removed a distinguishing query tag ("bulk=true") for signed ephemeral URLs under a new proxy optimization. The rate-limiter uses canonical route + credential fingerprint to attribute requests to quota lanes. With the tag stripped, bulk requests were hashed into the same priority-lane bucket as interactive traffic.
- Secondary factor: ephemeral-key fanout created many low-cardinality keys within the same refill window which amplified perceived token consumption on the priority lane.
- Evidence: ingress traces show identical canonical_route value for interactive and bulk requests during the spike; token-accounting logs show priority-lane debit entries matching embed upload request IDs.
- Impact quantification: ~4.5k 429s during the 90-minute window, estimated 7% increase in bulk job completion time for that day's runs.
- Temporary mitigation: server-side remap to attribute ephemeral key namespace to background lane for tenant. This reduced observed 429 rate from ~8-12% to <1% for the affected window.
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-12 16:30 UTC): tenant-level lane remapping for ephemeral key namespace.
Planned permanent fix: rate-limiter/edge patch to preserve route tagging for signed URLs and to prefer explicit credential namespace when computing lane attribution. Patch merged to staging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/487.
Rollout notes: patch will be deployed to canary, then us-west, with traffic shadowing for 2 hours. Post-deploy verification steps: monitor priority_lane_refill_rate, 429 rate for tenant, and total token burn for 2x baseline windows.
Customer workaround (if similar patterns recur): 1) Use explicit credential namespace mapping in Console (Settings -> Rate Pools) to isolate bulk worker keys into background pool. 2) Stagger ephemeral key rotation to avoid mass fanout within a single refill window.
follow_up_actions:
- Engineering: Complete canary rollout of canonicalization fix (owner: Samir Gupta). Target date: 2026-03-14.
- SRE: Add an alert for 'priority_lane_token_burn > 3x baseline in 1m for a single tenant' and a dashboard panel to show per-credential token attribution (owner: Miguel Torres).
- Support/Docs: Publish a short KB article 'Credential namespaces and rate-pool isolation' with recommended rotation patterns and Console steps (owner: Asha Patel).
- Product: Consider Console UX to surface credential-to-pool mapping during key creation to avoid accidental misclassification (product ticket suggested: INT-9833).
- Postmortem: Prepare a 1-page postmortem if customer impact reoccurs after patch (owner: Miguel Torres).
